Proposition
[Induced Homomorphisms] ↗ UNRESOLVED:chB:7.24 ↗ UNRESOLVED:chB:7.26 1. chA:A.6

Suppose $M$ and $N$ are topological spaces and $p \in M$. If $F: M \to N$ is a continuous map, then the map $F_*: \pi _1(M, p) \to \pi _1(N, F(p))$ defined by $F_*([\alpha ]) = [F \circ \alpha ]$ is a group homomorphism called the homomorphism induced by $F$. If $F$ is a homeomorphism, then $F_*$ is an isomorphism.

A topological space $M$ is said to be simply connected if it is path-connected and for some (hence every) point $p \in M$, the fundamental group $\pi _1(M, p)$ is trivial.

A continuous map $F: M \to N$ is said to be a homotopy equivalence if there is a continuous map $G: N \to M$ such that $G \circ F$ and $F \circ G$ are both homotopic to identity maps.
